content.thinking:
This dry, jargon-heavy methodology framing mainly targets the competence dimension of trust, likely boosting it modestly (~+1.6) while doing little for benevolence or openness — the technical density could even hurt comprehension. I'd estimate trust_post rising around +1.0 with anchoring effects, and distrust_post dropping roughly -0.9.

Moving through the remaining outcomes, I'm setting funding perceptions and institutional trust as modest gains (+0.4 and +0.6), belief_post around +0.7 since rigor bolsters credibility, and small positive nudges for concern, policy_general, and policy_specific (+0.4, +0.3, +0.2). Behavioral and donation effects stay tiny (+0.2, +0.04), newsletter signup negligible. Since this seems to be one of two jargon-heavy measurement/modeling variants, I'll settle on trust_multidimensional = 1.5.

parsed_output.reasoning_summary: This arm is a process-transparency/methodological-rigor message: it names real scientists and describes instruments (disdrometers), data collection, and statistical modeling, concluding that the methodology yields reproducible, empirically grounded knowledge. Its most proximal target is the competence dimension of trust (and secondarily integrity/objectivity), so I expect a modest positive effect on the fresh multidimensional trust battery (~1.5 points), concentrated in competence; benevolence and openness are barely addressed, and the heavy jargon (stereoplotters, support vector machines, wavelet analysis) may feel distancing to some readers, capping the effect below that of vivid narrative or messenger-based arms. The re-asked single items (trust_post, belief_post) are anchored by pre-treatment responses, so I shrink them relative to the primary battery, with distrust falling a bit less than trust rises (asymmetric, since distrust is a floor-heavy item). Downstream outcomes get progressively smaller effects: institutional trust is diluted by the federal-government item; funding perceptions and concern move slightly via credibility spillover; policy and behavior intentions move under half a point; the emphasis on scientists as objective, apolitical measurers gives essentially no push (perhaps a hair) on scientists' policy role. Incentivized outcomes get near-zero effects, with a very slight nudge on the AMS donation because the text foregrounds meteorological measurement.
